species.label: M. pneumoniae
species.plain: A small bacterium of the human airways with 688 proteins in its genome record, audited beside JCVI-syn3A for measured data to validate Cells against; the units of the law inventory are machines of animal cells, and it has none of them.

method: The organism's proteins are the 688 protein products of one frozen genome annotation, GenBank U00089.2: the genome of strain M129 as its submitters re-annotated it in 2000. UniProtKB holds a reviewed entry for 687 of them, and UniProt's archive (UniParc) holds all 688 sequences letter for letter, with the family signatures on each.
Licences were read before anything was copied; each is stated in sources, and what was read but not copied is in not_copied.
Each unit's family was taken from its own human candidates, by the same InterPro signatures that the planarian and Syn3A atlases ask. The build checks that the candidates carry them.
Each signature was looked for on all 688 sequences. None was found, for any unit.
A control for every zero: the same signature was asked of the UniProtKB entries of all mollicutes, the class of bacteria the organism belongs to; each unit's note gives what came back.

Eight further signatures, of the channels a bacterium could have (potassium, chloride, magnesium, water and membrane-stretch channels), were looked for as well. Seven were not found, although each is carried by UniProtKB entries of other mollicutes. One was: the family of water and glycerol channels, on the glycerol facilitator GlpF.

Under extra are nine of the organism's own membrane machines that bear on what the atlas draws and match no unit. Each has a reviewed UniProtKB entry of this strain and is listed by it; their functions are assigned by curators from sequence, not measured in this organism.
No similarity search was run, and nothing is called an ortholog.

not_copied: No sequence is copied: they stay with the downloads, outside the repository. The papers with measured protein amounts and other tables of this organism (Maier and others 2011, Wodke and others 2013, Chen and others 2016) are under non-commercial licences: nothing is taken from them, and the species file names the first two as places to read. What the files say of amounts, energy and food rests on open papers instead. Of the genome-scale models of the organism, only the open one of 2020 was read, for two statements.

U01.note: None of the 688 protein products of its genome carries the signature of voltage-gated sodium channel alpha subunits and sodium channel beta subunits (IPR001696, IPR027098, IPR000920). No UniProtKB entry of any mollicute, the class of bacteria it belongs to, carries them either. The unit's human candidates carry them, so the search finds the family where it exists. No ion channel of any family searched was found in this organism: its ions cross the membrane through transporters and pumps.

extra.name: ATP synthase, F1 alpha subunit
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_600, product "ATP synthase alpha chain" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "ATP synthase subunit alpha", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR000194 (ATPase, F1/V1/A1 complex, alpha/beta subunit, nucleotide-binding domain).
extra.why: Part of the cell's F-type ATP synthase, which sits in its one membrane; four of its subunits are listed here. A model of the cell's metabolism published in 2020 has this machine run in reverse, spending ATP to pump protons out; that is the model's result, not a measurement. The law inventory has no F-type ATPase.

extra.name: ATP synthase, F1 beta subunit
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_598, product "ATP synthase beta chain" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "ATP synthase subunit beta", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR000194 (ATPase, F1/V1/A1 complex, alpha/beta subunit, nucleotide-binding domain).
extra.why: The other subunit of the ATP synthase's catalytic head.

extra.name: ATP synthase, F0 c subunit
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_603, product "ATP synthase C chain" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "ATP synthase subunit c", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR000454 (ATP synthase, F0 complex, subunit C).
extra.why: The ring of the ATP synthase that carries protons across the membrane.

extra.name: ATP synthase, F0 a subunit
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_604, product "ATP synthase A chain" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "ATP synthase subunit a", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR000568 (ATP synthase, F0 complex, subunit A).
extra.why: The membrane subunit of the ATP synthase beside the ring, where protons enter and leave.

extra.name: P-type ATPase
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_209, product "cation-transporting P-type ATPase" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "Probable cation-transporting P-type ATPase", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR001757 (P-type ATPase).
extra.why: A pump of the same superfamily as the sodium-potassium and calcium pumps of animal cells. Its sequence carries the superfamily's signature and none of the signatures of those pumps' branches, so which ion it moves is not known here. It is the only P-type ATPase in the genome.

extra.name: Potassium uptake protein KtrB-like
extra.role: membrane part of a potassium uptake system
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_460, product "KtrB" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "Uncharacterized cation transporter MG322 homolog", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR003445 (Cation transporter).
extra.why: The membrane part of what the genome record calls the cell's potassium uptake system, KtrAB. That is how a cell without a sodium-potassium pump or a potassium channel would take up potassium; UniProt's curators leave the protein uncharacterised.

extra.name: Potassium uptake protein KtrA-like
extra.role: regulatory part of a potassium uptake system
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_461, product "KtrA, K+ Na+ uptake" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "Uncharacterized protein MG323 homolog", with UniProt's level of evidence "predicted": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR006037 (Regulator of K+ conductance, C-terminal).
extra.why: The cytoplasmic partner that the genome record gives the potassium uptake system.

extra.name: Glucose transporter PtsG
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_207, product "PTS system, glucose-specific IIABC component" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "PTS system glucose-specific EIICBA component", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR003352 (Phosphotransferase system, EIIC).
extra.why: The membrane part of the system that brings in glucose, the cell's main fuel. Its ATP comes from fermenting that sugar.

extra.name: Glycerol facilitator GlpF
extra.evidence_note: Locus MPN_043, product "glycerol uptake facilitator" in the genome record. Its reviewed UniProtKB entry names it "Probable glycerol uptake facilitator protein", with UniProt's level of evidence "inferred from homology": the entry is curated, and its function is assigned from its sequence, not measured in this organism. The sequence carries IPR000425 (Major intrinsic protein).
extra.why: The one channel-like protein found here: a member of the family of water and glycerol channels, annotated as the cell's glycerol uptake facilitator. It is not an ion channel, and the law inventory has no unit for it; its water permeability unit is a lumped property with no protein.
